In clear weather, pilots use the visual flight rules, or VFR. They look at the ground and use a map, a compass, and landmarks like cities, lakes, hills, rivers, roads, or forests to guide them.

When the weather is bad and they can’t see the ground, pilots use the instrument flight rules, or IFR. They rely on radio instruments, such as VOR or GPS, and instructions from air traffic control to keep them on course.

Under VFR, pilots choose big visible points on the map before the flight. While in the air, they look for those points to stay on track. The weather must be good enough so they can see the ground. They should not fly into clouds, because they can get lost.
